lessons.title: Lesson 1 — Hello, do you understand?
lessons.goal: Greet someone politely and say whether you speak or understand a language

steps.n: Listen to this conversation between an American man and a French woman who have just met.

steps.t: Bonjour, madame. Excusez-moi, vous parlez anglais ?
Non, monsieur. Je ne parle pas anglais.

steps.n: In the next few minutes you will learn to say all of that yourself. Let's begin with 'hello', which in French also means 'good morning' and 'good day'.
Listen and repeat.
Once more, 'hello'.
In France you always greet before anything else. Walking into a shop or up to a counter without saying hello is considered rude.
Here is how to say 'madam'. Listen and repeat.
Now put it together: 'hello, madam'. Listen, then repeat.
Here is how to say 'sir'. Listen and repeat.
Here is how to say 'excuse me'. Listen and repeat.
Here is how to say 'English, the language'. Listen and repeat.
Here is how to say 'you speak'. Listen and repeat.
Now put it together: 'do you speak English?'. Listen, then repeat.
Notice that in French you can turn a statement into a question just by raising your voice at the end. 'You speak English' and 'Do you speak English?' use exactly the same words.
Now put it together: 'excuse me, do you speak English?'. Listen, then repeat.
Here is how to say 'no'. Listen and repeat.
Here is how to say 'I don't speak'. Listen and repeat.
To make a sentence negative, French wraps the verb in a sandwich: one little word before it and one after it. You just heard that sandwich.
Now put it together: 'I don't speak English'. Listen, then repeat.
Now put it together: 'No, sir. I don't speak English.'. Listen, then repeat.

steps.t: Non, monsieur. Je ne parle pas anglais.

steps.expect: Non, monsieur. Je ne parle pas anglais.

steps.t: Non, monsieur. Je ne parle pas anglais.

steps.n: Here is how to say 'you understand'. Listen and repeat.
Here is how to say 'French, the language'. Listen and repeat.
Now put it together: 'do you understand French?'. Listen, then repeat.
Here is how to say 'yes'. Listen and repeat.
Here is how to say 'a little'. Listen and repeat.
Now put it together: 'yes, a little'. Listen, then repeat.
Here is how to say 'I don't understand'. Listen and repeat.
That last phrase is one of the most useful you will ever learn. Say it with a smile and most people will slow down and help you.

steps.q: Someone asks whether you speak English, and you want to say that you don't. What do you say?
A woman greets you in the morning. Greet her back politely.

steps.n: Say 'yes, a little'.
Ask a woman if she understands French.
Say that you don't understand.
Say 'excuse me, do you speak English?'
Answer: 'no, sir, I don't speak English.'

steps.expect: Non, monsieur. Je ne parle pas anglais.

steps.t: Non, monsieur. Je ne parle pas anglais.

steps.n: Ask 'do you understand French?'
Answer 'yes, a little'.
Now listen to the conversation from the beginning once more. You should understand every word.

steps.n: Try to take part. You are the man. Greet the woman and ask if she speaks English.

steps.t: Bonjour, madame. Excusez-moi, vous parlez anglais ?

steps.n: Now ask if she understands French.
Well done. That is the end of lesson one. In the next lesson you will learn to say thank you and please, and to say where you are from.

lessons.title: Lesson 2 — Thank you, and you?
lessons.goal: Exchange pleasantries, say please and thank you, and say your nationality

steps.n: Listen to this short conversation. A French woman runs into an American man she met yesterday.

steps.t: Ça va bien, merci. Et vous ?
Très bien, merci. Vous êtes américain ?
Oui, je suis américain. Au revoir, madame !

steps.n: You will be able to say all of this in a few minutes. But first, let's see what you remember from lesson one. Say 'hello, madam'.
Say 'excuse me, do you speak English?'
Say that you don't understand.
Now here is the friendliest question in French: 'how's it going?' Listen and repeat.
The same two words, said without the rising tone, are also the answer: 'it's going fine'. French people say them dozens of times a day.
Here is how to say 'very well'. Listen and repeat.
Here is how to say 'thank you'. Listen and repeat.
Here is how to say 'and you?'. Listen and repeat.
Now put it together: 'it's going well, thank you. And you?'. Listen, then repeat.

Now put it together: 'are you American?'. Listen, then repeat.
Here is how to say 'I am'. Listen and repeat.
Now put it together: 'I am American'. Listen, then repeat.
A woman says it slightly differently. The ending sounds like 'ken'. Listen and repeat.
Most French words that describe people have a masculine and a feminine form. Men say the short form, women add the final sound. You will hear this again and again.
Here is how to say 'French, said about a woman'. Listen and repeat.
Now put it together: 'are you French? Asking a woman.'. Listen, then repeat.
Say 'I am American' as a man would.
Now as a woman would.

Literally this means 'if it pleases you'. In France, please and thank you are not optional. Use them every single time.
Here is how to say 'a lot, very much'. Listen and repeat.
Now put it together: 'thank you very much'. Listen, then repeat.
Here is how to say 'you're welcome, literally 'it's nothing''. Listen and repeat.

Say 'please'.
